key_inference_review.claim: Factorial iterates eventually stabilize at each point.
key_inference_review.assessment: Valid. Finite orbit gives a periodic tail with threshold a and period p. Once k!>=a and p divides k!, all later factorial exponents are in that tail and congruent modulo p, so their values coincide. The threshold is explicitly point dependent.

key_inference_review.claim: The stabilized value is periodic and the residual is locally nilpotent.
key_inference_review.assessment: Valid. T^p fixes the tail value and p divides k!, so T^(a+k!)x=T^a x. Thus the exact two membership conditions hold.

key_inference_review.claim: The pointwise eventual-value operator is R-linear.
key_inference_review.assessment: Valid. For addition, choose a common stabilization index for x,y,x+y; for scalar multiplication choose one for x,rx. Each factorial power is R-linear, so the identities pass to the eventual values. This uses only finitely many thresholds, never a uniform threshold on M.

key_inference_review.claim: N_T and P_T are submodules with zero intersection.
key_inference_review.assessment: Valid. Common annihilating exponent max(m,n) and common periodic exponent pq prove additive closure. Zero/scalar closure are immediate from linearity of powers, including additive inverses via -1, and do not require new assumptions. A positive multiple kp>=n gives z=T^(kp)z=0 in the intersection, including n=0.

key_inference_review.claim: Direct sum, uniqueness, kernel, image and idempotence.
key_inference_review.assessment: Valid. Existence of decomposition plus the zero intersection establishes the actual internal direct sum; its addition map (n,p)↦n+p is therefore a linear isomorphism, with inverse x↦(x-e_Tx,e_Tx). This standard content is already established by the direct-sum assertion, so separately spelling out the two maps is not a missing obligation. key_inference_review.assessment: Valid. T preserves periodicity by commuting with its powers. The kernel argument proves injectivity. T^(p-1)z is periodic and maps to z, proving surjectivity; p=1 is permitted. The inverse of a bijective R-linear map is R-linear, with no global period assumption.
